actions.description: Capture a single image from a named camera with a declared resolution and exposure and return an image artifact reference.

inputs.description: Select one declared image source; each capture is independent.
inputs.name: camera

actions.name: capture_image

facts.text: The node declares the image_topic parameter with the absolute default '/image/image_raw'.
The node declares the camera_info_topic parameter with the absolute default '/image/camera_info'.
The module imports Image, CompressedImage and CameraInfo from sensor_msgs.msg.
The node creates a sensor_msgs Image publisher on image_topic_ with queue size 5 and a CameraInfo publisher on camera_info_topic_ with queue size 5.
The node declares the frame_id parameter with the literal default 'camera'.
image_callback calls get_time_msg and passes the result with the frame to get_image_msg.
get_time_msg fills builtin_interfaces Time sec and nanosec from the node clock's seconds_nanoseconds().
get_image_msg converts the frame with CvBridge().cv2_to_imgmsg(image, encoding='bgr8').
get_image_msg sets header.stamp to its time argument and header.frame_id to self.frame_id_.
image_callback publishes CameraInfo only when self.calib is truthy, then publishes the Image.
get_camera_info fills CameraInfo width, height, distortion_model and d, k, r and p from the calibration YAML.
get_compressed_msg constructs a CompressedImage and sets format 'jpeg'.
For video mode the node creates a timer with period 1.0/video_fps and registers image_callback.

In CameraSimulator.__init__, when type is not 'video', the node publishes every .jpg, .jpeg or .png file of the folder in natural-sort order without a timer and then logs that all images have been published.
In video mode, when a read fails and loop is false, image_callback cancels the timer, destroys the node and calls exit(); when loop is true it rewinds to 0 ms and reads again.
main constructs CameraSimulator and only then calls rclpy.spin.
The README describes the package as a ROS2 python node that streams video files or folder images to a topic and is used as a camera simulator.
The README documents supplying a camera calibration file to publish camera_info.

determinism.notes: Event-driven test peer with fixed placeholder packets; it does not replay captured traffic, advance a video, or model the upstream timer

fidelity.engine: analytic:ROS-free controlled peer (no video decode, no ROS graph)
gaps: the fake answers only the declared /image/image_raw subscription with a 4x2 placeholder BGR8 packet; it runs no ROS node, OpenCV, video decoder or camera
the upstream node publishes the decoded frame's own dimensions and declares no fixed resolution; the placeholder frame is smaller than a real video frame
the fake does not pace frames at the source video's FPS; the upstream interval is 1.0/video_fps (camera_simulator/camera_simulator.py:90-93)
the optional CameraInfo/calibration stream and the unused get_compressed_msg helper are outside this profile's selected image scope
transport, pixel and artifact bounds are client host policies, not camera resolution limits

in image-folder mode the node publishes every image once inside its constructor, before rclpy.spin and without a timer, so a rosbridge subscription opened later receives no frame, and in video mode without --loop the node exits at the end of the file; captures then fail MHS.DEVICE.NOT_READY (a probe with the topic silent failed after 2 s), so only a looping video gives repeatable captures
a capture waits for a fresh frame only up to the binding's default 2 s timeout, not the action's 10 s max_duration_ms, so a video slower than 0.5 fps fails NOT_READY
